author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
In an era where AI makes execution nearly free, the biggest risk to your career isn't being slow—it's being buried in legacy processes that prioritize planning over building.

1  ​Kill the Permission Loop: Stop waiting for buy-in when you can build a prototype in the time it takes to write the email.

2. ​Demo Over Decks: Stop selling ideas with slides; show a working product to force real decisions.

3. ​Embrace "Ugly" Shipping: Don't let the pursuit of 100% polish prevent you from getting the 80% that actually matters into the world.

4. ​Assume "Yes": Keep moving on your next task while waiting for feedback instead of letting your momentum stall.

5. ​Prototypes are the New Plans: Replace long-term strategy docs with rapid experiments that provide real-world data.

6. ​Ditch Default Meetings: Protect high-leverage build time by replacing alignment syncs with recorded demos.

7. ​Action Creates Consensus: Stop trying to get everyone to agree before you start; let the results of your work win them over.

8. ​Build in Public: Share your work early and often to avoid wasting weeks heading in the wrong direction.

​The bottleneck of knowledge work has moved from how fast you can execute to how much clarity and ambition you can bring to the table.
